title: Listed Investment Trusts Trading Policy

tiers.name: EQT Persons
tiers.description: Directors, key management personnel, and all employees of EQTHL and/or any of its wholly or majority owned companies including the Responsible Entity, and contractors and consultants who may come into the possession of Inside Information. Subject to Black-out Periods, the Trading Request Procedure, and the restricted-trading clearance regime for short-term trading, hedging and secured financing.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: The Responsible Entity's directors; a subset of EQT Persons distinguished by an additional post-trade disclosure obligation (nature, price and quantity traded) within 2 business days, to enable ASX reporting.

tiers.name: LIT Partners
tiers.description: Persons or entities engaged or contracted with the Responsible Entity to manage and/or administer a LIT. Must maintain their own trading policy, procedures and/or controls compliant with all relevant laws and enforcing Black-out Periods at least as strict as this Policy's, must disclose LIT Person transactions to the Company Secretary within 7 days, and must use the Trading Request Procedure for clause 6 restricted trading (short-term, hedging, margin lending/security).

tiers.name: LIT Persons
tiers.description: Directors, employees, contractors and consultants of a LIT Partner (or other related account as defined by the LIT Partner's trading policy). Trade under the LIT Partner's own trading policy for ordinary trades, but must use the Responsible Entity's Trading Request Procedure for clause 6 restricted trading.

tiers.name: Responsible Entity's Chair
tiers.description: Determines whether other exceptional circumstances (beyond hardship or a legal requirement) justify trading that would otherwise breach the Policy; where the Chair is the proposed trader, the EQTHL Board Risk Committee Chair performs this role instead.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A spouse, partner or child of an EQT Person (or LIT Person/Partner), or any other person the EQT Person may be expected to control or significantly influence, including other immediate family, business partners, companies or trusts. Must seek clearance through the relevant EQT Person, LIT Person or LIT Partner before trading.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Responsible Entity may specify any other period as a Black-out Period (Black-out Period limb (v)). Confidentiality of such a determination is not addressed. Where clauses (i), (ii) and (iii) overlap, the PDS/prospectus Black-out Period in clause (iii) prevails.

rules.detail: Unit is defined narrowly (a unit or other interest in a LIT, an option over an unissued unit, or a right to subscribe for a unit); Trade means to buy, sell or transfer any economic interest in Units. A third-party OTC derivative referencing Units that is not itself a risk-limiting/hedging arrangement is not caught by either definition, unlike a hedging-purpose derivative (see 'hedging').

A hedging or other financial arrangement that limits the economic risk of holding LIT Units (which would include a purchased put/written call collar) is not banned outright; it is permitted with prior written clearance obtained through the Trading Request Procedure.
rules.evidence: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding LIT Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

rules.detail: Monetisation (e.g. a prepaid forward) is not separately named but is a 'financial arrangement which operates to limit the economic risk' of holding Units, and so follows the same clearance regime as hedging under 6(ii).
rules.evidence: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding LIT Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the Policy; Trade is defined only as buying, selling or transferring an economic interest in Units.
Securities/Units lending is not named anywhere in the Policy.

CFDs are not named, but a CFD referencing Units used to offset or hedge exposure operates to limit the economic risk of holding the Units and so is caught by the same 6(ii) clearance regime as any other hedging arrangement.
rules.evidence: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding LIT Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

rules.detail: Margin lending is not banned outright; it is permitted with prior written clearance obtained through the Trading Request Procedure.
rules.evidence: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

rules.detail: Granting any form of security over Units is expressly permitted with prior written clearance through the Trading Request Procedure, not framed as a Dealing itself but as a separate restricted-trading category.
rules.evidence: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

rules.detail: The clause 6(iii) language ('margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units') is broad enough to cover any secured financing arrangement, not just a formal margin loan product; permitted with prior clearance.
rules.evidence: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

rules.detail: Trading in or out of Units on market within 3 months of acquiring them is not an absolute ban; it is permitted with prior written clearance through the Trading Request Procedure.
rules.evidence: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not engage in short-term or speculative trading in a LIT's Units, i.e. trading in or out of the Units on market within three (3) months of acquiring them, unless written prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.

financing_disclosure: all: trigger = before entering into margin lending or any arrangement granting security over Units; to the Responsible Entity's Company Secretary via the Trading Request Procedure for prior written clearance; deadline = before the arrangement is entered into.

external_documents: LIT Partner's own trading policy, procedures and/or controls, agreed with the Responsible Entity (referenced in clause 2, not reproduced in this document).
exemption_authority: The Responsible Entity's Chair (or the EQTHL Board Risk Committee Chair, for the Chair's own proposed trading) determines whether exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order/legal requirement, or other circumstances) justify trading that would otherwise breach the Policy, in consultation with the Company Secretary; any clearance remains subject to the overriding insider trading prohibition (clauses 5, 8).

bespoke_clauses.clause: EQT Persons, LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding LIT Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike an absolute ban, the put/call legs of a collar are achievable with prior written clearance, making this one of the more collar-friendly policies in the batch.

bespoke_clauses.clause: EQT Persons , LIT Persons, or LIT Partners may not enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Units, unless prior clearance to trade has been approved in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the Units is similarly achievable with prior clearance rather than banned outright.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The following types of trades ... are excluded from this policy: Those that do not result in a change to the beneficial interest in the Units ...; an acquisition of Units under the LIT's distribution reinvestment plan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike several peer policies, there is no express exclusion for a secured lender's enforcement sale on default, so a forced sale occurring during a Black-out Period risks being treated as a breach; the bank's default remedies need bespoke clearance planning.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance to trade is valid for five (5) business days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any clearance obtained for the hedge or loan legs lapses after 5 business days, requiring tight coordination of execution timing with the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: LIT Partners and LIT Persons may trade in a LIT's Units provided ... the trade has been executed in accordance with the LIT Partner's trading policy, procedures and/or controls which have been agreed with the Responsible Entity.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If administration of the LIT involves a LIT Partner, ordinary trades follow that partner's own policy, but the collar and loan (as clause 6 restricted trading) must still be cleared through the Responsible Entity's own Trading Request Procedure and Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where the Responsible Entity undertakes a buy-back of units in a LIT, the EQT Persons who have knowledge of the buy-back and are involved in the day to day management of the buy-back, are subject to a further Black-out Period commencing from the date the Responsible Entity makes the decision to buy-back the units in a LIT, to the next full business day after the buy-back has been completed.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Personnel managing a unit buy-back face an additional, event-driven blackout on top of the standard periodic Black-out Periods, further narrowing available execution windows for the collar.

bespoke_clauses.topic: Connected Persons clear through the EQT/LIT Person
bespoke_clauses.clause: a Connected Person must seek clearance through their EQT Person, LIT Person or LIT Partner in accordance with the Trading Request Procedure prior to trading in Units.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not avoid the regime, since the Connected Person must clear through the same EQT/LIT Person channel.

summary: Unlike many peer policies that ban hedging or secured financing outright, this Policy permits both with prior written clearance: clause 6(ii) allows a hedging or risk-limiting financial arrangement (covering a purchased put/written call collar) with clearance through the Trading Request Procedure, and clause 6(iii) similarly allows margin lending or any arrangement granting security over the Units with the same clearance. Both legs of a funded collar are therefore achievable in principle for EQT Persons (and, via the same procedure for restricted trading, LIT Persons and LIT Partners), subject to not holding Inside Information, trading outside the periodic and buy-back Black-out Periods, and outside the 3-month short-term trading restriction (itself also clearance-overridable). Clearance comes from the Responsible Entity's Company Secretary, lasts only 5 business days, can be refused or withdrawn without reasons, and any refusal must be kept confidential by the applicant; there is no express carve-out excusing a secured lender's enforcement sale from the Black-out Period regime, so default/enforcement mechanics need careful clearance and timing planning. Directors face an additional 2-business-day post-trade disclosure duty for ASX reporting, and Connected Persons must clear through the relevant EQT Person before trading, closing off indirect routes.
